points.description: States that a stack is a data structure (or abstract data type) that stores elements/items. Equivalent wording such as 'a collection of items' or 'a structure for holding data' earns the mark.

States the ordering property: the last item added is the first to be removed (last-in-first-out). Equivalent wording such as 'LIFO' or 'the most recently added item is removed first' earns the marks. Do not award this point if the answer describes a queue (first-in-first-out) or gives the order reversed.

deductions.description: Describing the stack as first-in-first-out or as a queue contradicts the LIFO property and loses the ordering mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks (5) for a answer that says a stack is a data structure holding elements and that the last item added is the first removed (or LIFO). Award 2 for the structure idea alone and 3 for the LIFO idea alone, since the answer has two separate ideas. Equivalent wording and the LIFO abbreviation are acceptable; the exact model wording is not required.
